meta.title: Raspberry Pi Prices and Lifecycle: Every Model Since 2012
meta.author: Philipp Schweizer, raspberry.tips
meta.price_definition: Official US list prices (MSRP) published by Raspberry Pi Ltd, excluding tax, duty and shipping. Street prices in other currencies including VAT are higher.
meta.source_policy: Primary sources only: raspberrypi.com news posts (date from article:published_time), product pages and product briefs / obsolescence notices on pip.raspberrypi.com. No retailer prices.

basis_values.stated: Absolute price appears verbatim in the source.
basis_values.calculated: Previous price + an increase stated in the source; 'confirmed' = the result also appears verbatim in a later source.
basis_values.assumption: Increase not stated for this product; taken from a general table or placed at an assumed date.
basis_values.approximate: Approximate figure, not a list price.
basis_values.delta_only: Only the increase/decrease is documented for this variant family; no absolute price.

status_values.active_no_date: In production, no end date published

meta.production_until_definition: Month of the official 'will remain in production until at least' statement (minimum, not an end date).

open_issues: Pi 500 / 500+ in February 2026: the post only says they 'are affected'. $130/$150 and $260/$280 are taken from the memory-density table (basis 'assumption'). The April 2026 end values are confirmed by product briefs.
Intermediate February 2026 values (Pi 4 4GB $75, 8GB $115; Pi 5 4GB $85, 8GB $125, 16GB $205) are calculated from stated increases; the chain is closed by the April 2026 product briefs.

Compute Module 4/5 historical variant prices are not published any more: older product-brief versions redirect to the current one. Only launch ranges, all increases and the current SKU lists are documented. Full histories exist only for CM4 1GB Lite and CM5 2GB Lite (forward-calculated, confirmed by the current briefs).
Compute Module 4 +$5 across-the-board increase: effective date unknown (before 12 Dec 2022); placed at 12 Dec 2022 as an assumption.
Compute Module 1: cut to $25 in 2017, then 'reduced by $5 to $25' in October 2025. An increase back to $30 in between is not documented; the October 2025 record is kept as 'no price change'.
Compute Module 5 16GB: launch date and launch price not found.
Compute Module 4S: only increases (deltas) are documented, no absolute list price; launch date only from secondary sources.
Not captured: Zero WH, Zero 2 WH, Pico 2 H/WH, Model A+ 512MB revision.

Current prices of Zero, Zero W, Zero 2 W, Pi 3B, Pi 3A+, Pi 1 B+/A+, CM3+ and the Picos are the last officially stated prices. The 2025/26 posts say older products were not affected, but the product pages could not be checked (Cloudflare) and the Zero 2 W brief has no price.
Pi 5: product page and October 2026 brief say January 2036, the news post of 17 Sep 2025 says January 2038.
Pi 500+ $410: taken from the research notes on the April 2026 product brief, not opened first-hand. Check before publishing.
CPI: $35 (2012) to about $51 (August 2026) is recalculated by build.py from BLS CPI-U values; the September 2026 value is due mid-October 2026.
Wayback snapshot links for the extension history were not re-checked (HTTP 429); spot-check before publishing.
Pi 1 Model B and CM4S launch dates rely on secondary sources; Compute Module 0 and SSD have no verified launch date.
Pi 3B+: product page January 2030 (confirmed first-hand 12 Oct 2026) vs. product brief and SBC guide January 2028.
